quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “panic”? (running and screaming when the fire alarm rings vs. walking to the field in a neat line)
quests.hint: Which choice helps everyone stay safe in a drill?
quests.explanation: To panic is to be so frightened you can’t think straight. To stay calm is to keep your head and follow the plan.
quests.funFact: Fire drills let people practice leaving a building safely.

quests.instruction: Zoya sank into the soft beanbag with a sigh, so comfortable. Two minutes on a wobbly wooden stool felt…
quests.hint: Compare a soft beanbag with a wobbly wooden stool after a few minutes.
quests.explanation: Comfortable means feeling relaxed and at ease. Uncomfortable means something is making you feel awkward or sore.
quests.funFact: The beanbag chair was designed in Italy in 1968.

quests.instruction: Asked what 6 × 7 is, Jai answered at once: 42, completely certain. Asked for the capital of a country he’d never heard of, he shrugged and said, “Hmm… I’m…”
quests.hint: Think about how sure you feel when you’re only guessing.
quests.explanation: Certain means you have no doubt. Unsure means you aren’t confident about the answer.
quests.funFact: Scientists often say “probably” instead of “definitely” when they aren’t completely certain.

quests.instruction: A new kid showed Lena a strange shell and asked a dozen questions about where it came from. Another child glanced at it and looked away. One was curious; the other was…
quests.hint: Which child wanted to know more?
quests.explanation: Curious people want to find out more. Uninterested people don’t care to.
quests.funFact: “Curiosity killed the cat” is an old saying that warns against being too nosy.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is the rude version of “Could I please have some water?”
options: May I get a drink of water?
quests.hint: Listen to the tone: no “please”, no “thank you”.
quests.explanation: The same request can sound polite or rude, depending on the words. Commands without “please” sound demanding.
quests.funFact: Many languages have polite and casual ways to say the same thing.

quests.instruction: Standing at the stream, Hari tested each stone before stepping, a cautious crossing. Meera bounded across without looking, which was…
quests.hint: Hari tests each stone; Meera bounds across without looking.
quests.explanation: Cautious people think about danger and take care. Reckless people rush in without thinking.
quests.funFact: Stepping stones are one of the oldest ways of crossing a stream.

quests.instruction: Ana thought pineapple on pizza sounded awful, but she tried a bite anyway and admitted it was good. Her brother crossed his arms and refused to even taste it. Ana was open-minded; he was…
quests.hint: Who wouldn’t change their mind at all?
quests.explanation: Open-minded people are willing to try new ideas. Stubborn people refuse to change their mind.
quests.funFact: Pineapple pizza was reportedly first served in Canada in 1962.

quests.instruction: Choosing a game, Ria announced, “We’re playing my game, and you’re all on my team.” Her friend said, “Whatever everyone wants is fine with me.” Ria was bossy; her friend was…
quests.hint: Picture who would say, “Whatever everyone wants is fine.”
quests.explanation: Bossy people insist on telling others what to do. Easygoing people are relaxed and flexible.
quests.funFact: Rock-paper-scissors is a popular way to decide things fairly.

quests.instruction: The new neighbors waved, smiled and brought sweets to say hello. They were friendly. A neighbor who never greets anyone and closes the door quickly seems…
quests.hint: Think of the neighbor who would bring you sweets and wave hello.
quests.explanation: Friendly people are warm and welcoming. Unfriendly people seem cold and distant.
quests.funFact: Greeting neighbors is a custom in many parts of the world.

quests.instruction: Dad promised to take Kabir to the cricket match and did exactly that. If he had cancelled for no good reason, he would have…
quests.hint: What happens to a promise that isn’t carried out?
quests.explanation: To keep a promise is to do what you said you would. To break it is to fail to do so.
quests.funFact: In some places, people seal a promise with a handshake or a pinky swear.

quests.instruction: Ria ate the last slice of cake. When Mum asks who ate it, which answer is the honest one?
quests.hint: Honest answers say what really happened.
quests.explanation: Honesty means telling what really happened, even when it’s awkward. The other answers try to hide it.
quests.funFact: In many courts, witnesses promise to tell the truth.

quests.instruction: After losing the final, Tara shook hands with the winners and said, “Well played!” She’s a good sport. A player who throws the ball and storms off is a…
quests.hint: Picture someone who throws the ball and storms off after losing.
quests.explanation: A good sport accepts winning and losing politely. A poor sport can’t.
quests.funFact: Many sports end with handshakes or high-fives between the teams.

quests.instruction: Imran peeked at his neighbor’s cards during the game. That was cheating. His friend reminded him to…
quests.hint: What does everyone need to do for a game to be fair?
quests.explanation: Cheating breaks the rules to get an advantage. Playing fair means following them like everyone else.
quests.funFact: Games have rules so that every player has the same chance.

quests.instruction: Two best friends had a big argument and stopped talking. They fell out. A week later, they said sorry and became friends again. They…
quests.hint: After an argument ends well, friends say sorry and start again.
quests.explanation: To fall out is to stop being friends after an argument. To make up is to become friends again.
quests.funFact: “Make up” has many meanings in English, such as inventing a story or becoming friends again.

quests.instruction: A window was broken during football. Dev saw it happen and said, “It was me.” A boy who wasn’t even there is innocent. Dev is…
quests.hint: Think about who is responsible for the broken window.
quests.explanation: Innocent means not responsible for what happened. Guilty means you did it.
quests.funFact: In many countries, a person accused of something is treated as innocent until it’s proven otherwise.

quests.instruction: Grandpa woke up on the wrong side of the bed and snapped at everyone, so he was grumpy. After his tea, he hummed and chatted with the neighbors. He was…
quests.hint: How does he sound once his mood has lifted?
quests.explanation: Grumpy means cross and easily annoyed. Pleasant means agreeable and nice to be around.
quests.funFact: Hunger and tiredness can make anyone grumpier.

quests.instruction: Drinking water and going to bed on time are healthy habits. Staying up until midnight on school nights is an…
quests.hint: Think about how you feel the next morning after a very late night.
quests.explanation: Healthy habits help your body and mind. Unhealthy habits slowly cause problems.
quests.funFact: Both sleep and exercise help your body and brain.

quests.instruction: At the park, which child is acting the opposite of selfish?
quests.correctAnswer: Dhruv lets his friends take turns with his new ball.
options: Dhruv lets his friends take turns with his new ball.
Dhruv sits on the swing by himself.
Dhruv hides his new ball inside his bag.
quests.hint: Look for the child who’s thinking about others, not just himself.
quests.explanation: Selfish people keep things for themselves. The opposite is sharing, like letting friends take turns.
quests.funFact: Taking turns is one of the first social rules children learn.

quests.instruction: On Saturday, Neel biked, played tag and swam: a very active day. On Sunday, he sat in a chair and did nothing at all: an…
quests.hint: Which day left him with no sweat at all?
quests.explanation: Active means moving and doing things. Idle means doing nothing.
quests.funFact: Health experts suggest children get about an hour of physical activity every day.

quests.instruction: The farmers worked from dawn until noon. After lunch, they sat under the neem tree to…
quests.hint: After a long morning of effort, bodies ask for a break under a shady tree.
quests.explanation: To work is to put in effort. To rest is to stop and recover.
quests.funFact: Lions rest for most of the day and save their energy for hunting.

quests.instruction: Which comment is the opposite of kind: “Nice try, you’ll get it next time!”?
quests.hint: Picture how the player feels after each comment.
quests.explanation: Kind words lift someone up after a mistake. Mean words push them down.
quests.funFact: Words can hurt feelings, which is why people say “think before you speak”.

quests.instruction: Aunt Maya offers a plate of laddoos. If you want one, you say, “Yes, please.” If you’re full, you politely say…
quests.hint: Which reply refuses without being rude?
quests.explanation: “Yes, please” accepts politely. “No, thank you” declines politely.
quests.funFact: In Hindi, “nahin, dhanyavaad” means “no, thank you”.

quests.instruction: When Rani arrived at her new school, the teacher and the children gave her a warm welcome. If they had all turned their backs and refused to speak to her, she would have gotten the…
quests.hint: It’s an idiom, so it has nothing to do with actual temperature or shoulders.
quests.explanation: A warm welcome is a friendly greeting. The cold shoulder is an idiom for being ignored.
quests.funFact: Idioms like “cold shoulder” don’t literally have anything to do with shoulders or temperature.

quests.instruction: When the ball hit the wrong goal, Anil threw down his cap and shouted. His teammate took a deep breath and said, “Let’s try again.” Anil was hot-headed. His teammate was…
quests.hint: One teammate throws down his cap; the other takes a deep breath.
quests.explanation: Hot-headed people lose their tempers quickly. Cool-headed people stay calm.
quests.funFact: English idioms often use heat and cold to describe feelings, like “hot-tempered” and “ice-cold”.

quests.instruction: Before the cricket match, it began to drizzle. Anya said, “The rain will stop soon and we’ll still play!” Her friend said, “It’ll rain all day and ruin everything.” Anya was optimistic; her friend was…
quests.hint: Which friend expects the worst?
quests.explanation: Optimistic people expect good things. Pessimistic people expect bad ones.
quests.funFact: “Optimism” comes from a Latin word meaning “the best”.

quests.instruction: Zara waited outside the doctor’s room, feeling anxious about her check-up. When the doctor said everything was fine, she felt…
quests.hint: Imagine the doctor says “everything is fine” and your worry melts away.
quests.explanation: Anxious means uneasy about what might happen. Relieved means the worry has gone.
quests.funFact: A big breath out is often called a “sigh of relief”.

quests.instruction: Which pair of words are opposites?
quests.hint: Look for the two words that sit at opposite ends of a feeling.
quests.explanation: Brave and frightened describe opposite reactions to danger. The other pairs are close in meaning.
quests.funFact: Thesauruses group words by meaning, and many also list their antonyms.

quests.instruction: Kavin was asked to water the class plant every Friday and never forgot, so he’s responsible. A classmate who leaves the tap running and walks away is…
quests.hint: Who can you trust to do a job properly?
quests.explanation: Responsible people do their duties and care about the results. Irresponsible people don’t.
quests.funFact: Plants need water, light and air to grow.

quests.instruction: In football practice, Hari kept the ball all game and never passed. The coach said, “Stop hogging the ball and…”
quests.hint: On a team, the ball is meant to move around, not stay with one player.
quests.explanation: Hogging means keeping something for yourself. Sharing means giving others a turn.
quests.funFact: Football is called soccer in some countries and is played by millions of people worldwide.

quests.instruction: Riya says, “I love this song!” Which reply shows the opposite opinion?
quests.hint: Look for the reply that disagrees with “I love this song.”
quests.explanation: To disagree is to hold a different opinion. “I can’t stand it” is the reverse of “I love this”.
quests.funFact: Music has been part of human life for tens of thousands of years.
